key_insight: Variational functional neural networks (vfNN) find physical states by optimizing continuum functionals directly rather than solving their Euler–Lagrange differential equations.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a route to physics-based neural solvers using lower-order derivatives and physical scales instead of ad hoc loss weights.
method: Represent system states with a neural network and optimize an integral-form physical functional.
Use lower-order derivatives and physically grounded scales rather than conventional PINN residual losses.
Combine quasi-Newton optimization with simulated annealing to target solutions regardless of their stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate simulations on benchmark systems governed by linear and nonlinear ordinary differential equations, without quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Nonconvex optimization and unstable stationary solutions complicate convergence; broader performance beyond the reported ODE benchmarks remains unestablished.
